This is round2ReviewFoundGap's exact shape, reopened for the fix that was supposed to close it — of the four links in DrawRoomLabel's chain (rockTiles into DrawRoomLabels; BordersWallToNorth branch; labelTop from LabelTop(purposeInset); labelTop into the draw calls), only the first and last were guarded before this round.

round3LabelWiringGap.closure: Two new tests, mirroring the border-side pair exactly: Main_DrawRoomLabel_computes_labelTop_from_the_picked_inset (whitespace-normalised Assert.Contains for 'RoomGeometry.LabelTop(purposeInset)', since AdapterSource.CallsTo cannot see this call — it is qualified on RoomGeometry, not the adapter itself, the same reason CallsTo cannot see RoomGeometry.Border either; verified empirically before writing the test: AdapterSource.CallsTo(body, "LabelTop") returns zero calls against DrawRoomLabel's real body, so a literal CallsTo-based assertion would be permanently red rather than a working guard) and Main_DrawRoomLabel_branches_on_BordersWallToNorth (identical technique to Main_DrawRoomBorder_branches_on_BordersWallToNorth). All four links in DrawRoomLabel's chain are now guarded.

round3UnitsMismatch.description: Independent review round 3, N3: The_label_block_still_fits_one_cell_at_the_deepest_wall_adjacent_inset compared a reference-pixel quantity (labelBottom, max 18.0) against 32 — the real screen-pixel minimum tile size ADR 0008 allows, not the reference tile size the quantity is actually measured against. The same units mismatch review named in round 1 against Wall_adjacent_insets_are_still_distinct_and_bounded's 32 / 4.0 bound.
round3UnitsMismatch.fix: 32 -> 22.0 (CameraView.ReferenceTileSize, private at CameraView.cs:108, restated as a local const with that provenance in the test). Margin at the true ceiling: 18.0 against 22.0 is 82% of the reference cell, 4.0 reference px of margin — against the old (wrong) 32 the bound was live only 45% over budget; against the corrected 22 it is live 18% over, which is the sensitivity the test's own name promises.
round3UnitsMismatch.thirdPlaceCheck: Swept tests/DungeonFortress.Presentation.Tests/RoomGeometryTests.cs and src/DungeonFortress.Presentation/RoomGeometry.cs for every remaining literal 32 or 48. Two occurrences of the identical `32 / 4.0` pattern remain, both InRange bounds comparing a reference-pixel inset against the same screen-pixel-derived ceiling: line 178 (Two_purposes_next_to_each_other_do_not_share_a_border_line, checking the plain BorderInset — predates this issue, from Issue #52) and line 417 (Wall_adjacent_insets_are_still_distinct_and_bounded, checking WallAdjacentBorderInset — the one review named in round 1). No third, previously unnamed place exists; RoomGeometry.cs itself contains no tile-size literal at all (it is reference-pixel throughout, by construction). Neither of the two known occurrences was touched this round: round 3 named exactly two mechanical edits (N1, N3) and the task explicitly excludes redoing anything already closed.
